productLoss: Lynx rendered an oversized bordered project card with project title, absolute path, file count, and a text Refresh button where the production Web Files browser uses a fixed compact subheader.
The file tree used 28px rows, 12px rounding, and 11px monospace labels instead of the Web Files authority's 24px rows, 5px rounding, and 12px sans labels.
The toolbar and tree shared one scroll surface, the search control was absent, and folder/file rows lacked the production Files browser icon treatment.
The first production build showed that Lynx strips :focus-within, so the new search control initially lacked the intended Native focus feedback.
harnessMismatch: The first strict Native run queried the computed border-radius shorthand. Lynx DevTool returned 0px even though the encoded scoped rule followed the shared 12px rule and all four computed corner longhands were 5px.
The final verifier reads border-top-left-radius, border-top-right-radius, border-bottom-right-radius, and border-bottom-left-radius independently and requires all four values to be 5px.
classification.evidenceBoundary: Web source owns the Files browser anatomy and exact compact dimensions. This exact-bundle Native run proves measured touch reachability, real indexed content, geometry, typography, corner radii, transport, zero renderer errors, screenshot dimensions, and cleanup. No same-snapshot Web Files screenshot exists in this run, so the Native screenshot is representative evidence and is not claimed as matched Web pixel parity. Physical keyboard search input remains pending-user-session; the source contract proves that bindinput feeds getProjectFilePickerMatches and rebuilds the filtered tree.
